blocks.text: Greece and Jordan are an unusual pairing, and that is part of what makes the trip interesting. Athens and Petra may both be known for their history, but they feel nothing alike. Add Delphi, Wadi Rum, or a few days on the Greek islands and the contrast becomes even stronger.

Our Greece & Jordan Tours range from 8 to 13 days, with three routes built around different priorities. One keeps the journey focused on Athens and Jordan, another adds Delphi and Wadi Rum for a stronger archaeological and cultural route, while the longest itinerary includes Mykonos and Santorini before continuing to Jordan.

Depending on the tour, arrangements can include hotels, guided sightseeing with local guides, airport and hotel transfers, regional flights, transportation within Jordan, and Greek ferry or domestic flight connections where specified.

Greece & Jordan Route Planning • Athens–Amman Connections • Greek Island Logistics on Selected Tours • Private Transportation in Jordan • Petra & Wadi Rum Arrangements • Local Support in Both Countries
The shorter route keeps Greece centered on Athens before continuing to Jordan. It works well when the Acropolis and Petra are the two experiences you most want to build the trip around.
Adding Delphi and Wadi Rum changes the journey. Delphi extends the archaeological side of Greece beyond Athens, while Wadi Rum introduces open desert and sandstone landscapes after Petra.

The longest route has a different rhythm altogether. Mykonos and Santorini add island scenery and independent time before the journey continues to Jordan. This option makes more sense when the Greek Islands are an important part of why you chose Greece, rather than places you feel you should include simply because you are nearby.

sections.heading: Athens and Petra: The Two Anchors

blocks.text: Athens and Petra sit naturally at the center of all three routes, but visiting them feels very different.

Athens brings the Acropolis and the historical layers of the Greek capital into a modern city stay. Petra is more immersive: you enter through the Siq on foot before reaching the Treasury and continuing into an archaeological landscape that extends well beyond its most famous monument.
For a shorter journey, concentrating on these two places can be more rewarding than trying to fit several additional destinations into eight days.

sections.heading: From Delphi to the Cyclades — and Petra to Wadi Rum

blocks.text: The additional stops are not simply there to make the longer tours longer.

Delphi is the natural addition when history and archaeology are the main focus in Greece. Mykonos and Santorini do something different, bringing coastal scenery and a slower stretch of the journey before Jordan.

The same principle applies after Petra. Wadi Rum is not another archaeological stop. Its desert landscapes give the Jordan section a different character and broaden the trip without adding another city.
This is why the routes should be compared by experience rather than by counting destinations.
Athens and Amman are the main gateways between Greece and Jordan, with the international connection normally made by air.

Routes that include only Athens or Athens and Delphi are relatively straightforward. When Mykonos and Santorini are added, ferry schedules or domestic flights need to work with the onward connection to Jordan.
Once in Jordan, the logistics are different. Travel between Amman, Petra, and Wadi Rum is mainly by road, making it easier to move between the principal stops without additional domestic flights.
April through June and September through October offer a good overall balance for sightseeing in Athens, Delphi, and Petra while also fitting the main Greek island travel season.

July and August suit travellers who place greater importance on Mykonos and Santorini, although Athens and Jordan will be hotter. Outside the main island season, an Athens and Delphi-focused route can offer more flexibility.

The choice between the three tours is therefore fairly simple: keep the journey focused on Athens and Petra, add Delphi and Wadi Rum for a stronger historical and landscape-focused route, or choose Mykonos and Santorini when the Greek Islands are an essential part of the trip.

For single-country travel, compare our Greece Tours or Jordan Tours. For a different two-country route involving Jordan, see our Turkey & Jordan Tours. Longer regional itineraries are available through our Egypt, Jordan & Israel Tours.

faqs.q: What are the highlights of a Greece and Jordan combined tour?
faqs.a: In Greece: the Acropolis with the Parthenon in Athens, caldera views at Oia in Santorini, and a caldera boat cruise. In Jordan: the Roman city of Jerash, Petra's 1.2-km Siq and Treasury facade, a 4x4 jeep safari in Wadi Rum, and a float in the Dead Sea at 430 metres below sea level.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Greece and Jordan?
faqs.a: Our Greece & Jordan tours currently range from 8 to 13 days. An 8-day itinerary focuses on Athens, Amman and Petra; a 10-day itinerary can add Delphi, Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea; and a 13-day itinerary allows time for Mykonos and Santorini before continuing to Jordan.

faqs.q: How much does a Greece and Jordan combined tour cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Our Greece & Jordan tours currently start from €1,795 per person. Prices vary according to the itinerary, travel dates, hotel category and services included. Please see the individual tour pages for current prices

faqs.q: Is the flight from Athens to Amman included?
faqs.a: The Athens–Amman flight inclusion varies by itinerary. Please check the Included and Excluded sections of the individual tour page, as international flight arrangements may differ between programs.

faqs.q: Do I need visas for both Greece and Jordan?
faqs.a: Visa requirements depend on nationality and may change. Travelers should check the latest official entry requirements for Greece and Jordan before departure. Our team can provide general guidance based on your itinerary.

faqs.q: Is the Jordan Pass worth buying for this tour?
faqs.a: The Jordan Pass may be useful if you plan to visit Petra and other included attractions. It offers one, two, or three days at Petra. Before buying, check your visa eligibility, required length of stay, and whether your tour already includes entrance fees.

faqs.q: Is Delphi or Olympia included in Greece and Jordan tours?
faqs.a: Delphi is included in our 10-day Greece and Jordan tour. Our 8-day tour focuses on Athens and Petra, while the 13-day tour adds Mykonos and Santorini. Olympia is not included in any of these three published itineraries, but we can add it to a customized tour if you would like to explore more of mainland Greece before continuing to Jordan.

faqs.q: How much walking does Petra require?
faqs.a: A standard Petra day covers 2 to 4 km from the visitor centre through the 1.2-km Siq to the Treasury and main monument area. The Monastery trail adds 3 km and 800 carved steps. Petra is not wheelchair accessible in most sections. Horses and donkeys are available for hire at the Siq entrance. Allow a full day minimum.

faqs.q: What accommodation is used in Greece and Jordan tours?
faqs.a: In Greece: 3 to 4-star hotels near the Plaka in Athens; boutique cliff-side hotels in Oia or Fira in Santorini. In Jordan: 4-star hotels in Amman; hotels in Wadi Musa village near Petra; a Bedouin camp in Wadi Rum for 1 night. Luxury upgrades are available throughout on request.

faqs.q: Can Greece and Jordan be extended to include Egypt or Israel?
faqs.a: Yes. Egypt, Jordan, and Israel combined tours add Cairo, the Pyramids, Nile cruise, and Jerusalem to the Jordan portion. Greece can serve as the starting point for that circuit. Contact us for a custom multi-country proposal.
